data.name: TMM: Entourage
data.detailed_description:
Description

Tales of Mystics and Madmen: Entourage or TMM: Entourage for short is a top down shooter with a couple of RTS mechanics mixed in. You pick one of three sides and fight either the other two in various competitive or just one side in cooperative game modes. Each player character is joined by three bodyguards which may be controlled by your friends at the push of a button on a gamepad. The game offers various objective-based game modes which vary in length and style, with most of them sharing the same principles.

Although this game can be played by yourself, it is more fun to engage in conflict with your friends locally and with others around the globe.

Background

Three sides fight for supremacy. They are called Primitivists, Progressionists and Royalist. The Prims are deeply connected with nature and draw influences from various African and Asian cultures. Progs have aristocratic origins and happen to be techno-lovers (literally), they tend to invent the next big thing before anyone else gains knowledge of their last big thing. The Royals foster nobility and pride and like to duel each other if not fighting off some bigger threat.

Key Features

  • PvP Game Modes: King of the Hill, Escort, Team Deathmatch, Warfare and more
  • PvE Game Modes: Stronghold, Onslaught, Tug of War and more
  • Each mode changes gameplay in some way
  • Leaderboard support for various Game Modes
  • Campaign Mode: Play increasingly difficult matches with your friends vs bots, progress between sessions is saved
  • Hotjoin local coop: Up to 4 players can play locally, three of them can join/leave at any time
  • Lead the charge as Commander, your bodyguards (Entourage) follow you
  • Change the appearance and weapons of your Commander and bodyguards during the match
  • Unique RTS/Shooter mix: control a single unit and build turrets directly, order troop movement indirectly and their composition
  • Invade the enemy's base to kill their workers reducing their income
  • Various weapons with primary and secondary fire modes unique to each faction
  • RPG mechanics to round up the gameplay: gain technology points by defeating enemies and empower your troops, use skills to buff your allies
  • Call and enter a gunship to turn the tide of battle
  • Procedural map generator: each game mode requires a different map layout, the map generator creates maps according to set rules
  • Match customization: there are various parameters which can be set to adjust game length, starting resources etc
  • New game modes and maps will be added at irregular intervals as free DLC

reviews.review:
TMM: Entourage is an unconventional tactical action game that combines real-time combat with battlefield leadership, offering an interesting alternative to traditional multiplayer shooters. Developed and published by Chocolate Ship Games, it places players in command of armed forces while allowing them to participate directly in the fighting. Rather than focusing entirely on individual combat skills, the game encourages strategic thinking, coordinated assaults, and effective troop management. Its ambition is immediately apparent, although the overall experience feels more like an experimental independent project than a fully polished military simulation. Despite its limitations, the combination of action and tactical decision-making provides a distinctive foundation that may appeal to players interested in lesser-known strategy games.

The central gameplay concept revolves around commanding soldiers while actively contributing to battlefield engagements. Players must consider troop positioning, offensive opportunities, and the importance of maintaining control over strategically valuable locations. This creates an interesting relationship between individual performance and collective effectiveness. Charging into combat without considering allied forces can undermine an otherwise promising attack, while careful coordination offers opportunities to gain an advantage. The game attempts to reward battlefield awareness rather than relying exclusively on reflexes. However, the tactical systems are relatively straightforward, and players expecting the sophistication of established military strategy titles may find the available options somewhat limited.

One of its more interesting mechanics involves supporting and motivating allied soldiers. Instead of presenting friendly units as background characters, the game incorporates them into its central combat philosophy. The idea of strengthening an organized fighting force gives encounters a sense of purpose beyond simply defeating opponents. Defensive construction further supports this approach by allowing players to establish positions that can influence engagements. Gunship assistance adds another tactical possibility, potentially changing the momentum of a confrontation when deployed effectively. These mechanics work toward creating a battlefield where preparation and coordination matter, although their effectiveness ultimately depends on the responsiveness of the game's systems.

Multiplayer represents an important part of the intended experience, with competitive and cooperative possibilities encouraging players to approach combat from different perspectives. Fighting alongside friends can make troop coordination more entertaining, particularly when participants communicate and develop strategies together. Local shared-screen functionality and online multiplayer broaden the available ways to participate, while Steam achievements, statistics, and leaderboards provide additional incentives. Unfortunately, the limited player population presents a considerable obstacle. Finding active opponents may prove difficult, and the experience becomes significantly less attractive when its multiplayer features cannot be used consistently. Having a dedicated group of friends would likely make the game considerably more enjoyable.

Visually, TMM: Entourage adopts a functional presentation that reflects its independent development background. Its environments and battlefield elements emphasize practical gameplay rather than cinematic spectacle. While this approach is understandable for a modest production, the overall presentation lacks the refinement expected from more accomplished action-strategy games. Clear visibility and readable unit positioning are particularly important in tactical combat, making visual communication essential to the experience. The sound design and general atmosphere also appear modest in scope. The result is a game whose underlying ideas are more memorable than its audiovisual execution, although players who prioritize mechanics over presentation may be more forgiving.

The game's greatest challenge is translating its promising combination of mechanics into consistently satisfying engagements. Managing soldiers, constructing defenses, and participating in combat can create enjoyable tactical situations, but the experience depends heavily on responsive controls and dependable unit behavior. Any inconsistency in movement or battlefield coordination becomes particularly noticeable when the player is responsible for directing multiple soldiers. The relatively modest scope also limits the amount of strategic variety available. Although there is room to experiment with different approaches, the gameplay may become repetitive for those seeking extensive customization, complex progression, or substantial mission diversity.

Replayability is closely connected to the multiplayer experience and the player's willingness to experiment with different combat strategies. Competitive encounters can introduce unpredictability, while cooperative play creates opportunities for coordinated tactics. Achievements and leaderboards offer additional objectives, but they cannot entirely compensate for a limited active community. The game is consequently better suited to occasional sessions with friends than prolonged competitive play. Its unusual combination of mechanics may initially generate curiosity, yet sustaining that interest requires players to appreciate its core gameplay despite the relatively narrow range of activities.

Regarding technical compatibility, the game provides support for Windows, macOS, and Linux, making it accessible across several desktop operating systems. Partial controller support is also advertised, although this does not necessarily guarantee an entirely comfortable controller-based experience. Steam Deck compatibility remains unverified, as an official Verified or Playable classification could not be confirmed. While Linux support suggests that running the game on Valve's handheld may be possible, compatibility, performance, and controller functionality should not be assumed. Players interested primarily in portable gaming should approach it cautiously until reliable Steam Deck testing becomes available.

Ultimately, TMM: Entourage is a game with worthwhile ideas but noticeable limitations. Its combination of direct combat, troop leadership, defensive construction, and battlefield support offers something different from conventional shooters. Unfortunately, limited multiplayer activity, modest production values, and uncertain mechanical refinement prevent those ideas from achieving their full potential. It remains an interesting curiosity for enthusiasts of experimental tactical games, especially those who can organize multiplayer sessions with friends. However, players expecting extensive content, sophisticated artificial intelligence, or highly polished combat mechanics may find the experience disappointing.

Its creative battlefield mechanics and emphasis on teamwork deserve recognition, but limited accessibility to active multiplayer matches and an uneven overall presentation make it a difficult recommendation beyond its niche audience.

Rating: 5/10
